blocks.h2: Plumbing Problems That Can't Wait in Geneva
blocks.intro: Call us right away for any of these:

tiles.body: A ceiling or wall that's bulging, stained or dripping. Shut off the water and stay out from under it.
Dirty water rising at the floor drain or basement toilet. Stop running water upstairs.
The pump has quit and the rain hasn't.
Close the cold water valve on top of the water heater.
Leave the house. Call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside.

tiles.h3: A Main Valve That Won't Close
tiles.body: Old valves can seize. Don't force it. Call us and we'll help get the water off.

blocks.h2: What Emergencies Look Like in Geneva
blocks.intro: Geneva's emergency calls tend to follow its housing: century-old homes near the river and newer homes to the west.

items.body: Older homes with little wall insulation see the most frozen and burst pipes when temperatures drop below zero. See [burst pipe repair](/geneva/burst-pipe-repair).

In September 2008, about 9 inches of rain fell on Geneva in two days. Heavy storms still bring backup calls from homes with gravity floor drains. See [sewage backup service](/geneva/sewage-line-backup-services).
A tank that splits can put dozens of gallons on the basement floor in minutes. See [water heater repair](/geneva/water-heater-repair).
In homes built after 1990, original sump pumps and water heaters tend to fail at the worst possible time.

items.q: How soon can a plumber get to my home in Geneva?
items.preview: Call any time. We'll give you an honest window.
items.answer: Call us any time. Our Campbell Street office is close to downtown Geneva. Arrival depends on the day and call volume, but we'll give you an honest window and get a plumber to you as soon as we can.

items.q: What if my main shutoff won't turn?
items.answer: Don't force it, because an old valve can break. Call us. We can shut off the water and replace the valve so the next emergency is easier to stop.

items.q: Water is coming through my plaster ceiling. What do I do?
items.preview: Shut off the water, cut power to that area and stay clear.
items.answer: Close the main water valve, turn off the breaker for lights in that ceiling and keep people out from under it. Put down buckets and call us.
